messages.content:
A learner of Spanish wrote this for Correo electrónico (readers: La Sra. Morales, de la escuela de idiomas a la que quiere aplicar). What they want to do: Solicitar plaza en el curso de septiembre y preguntar precios y alojamiento.
The post, sentence by sentence:
<<<
[S1] Estimada Sra.
[S2] Morales:

[S3] Mi nombre es Daniel y yo soy de Manchester, en Inglaterra.
[S4] Le escribo porque quiero solicitar plaza en el curso de septiembre.
[S5] Vengo a mejorar mi español: mi novia es de Granada, conocí a su familia el año pasado pero no entendí casi nada, y tengo muchas ganas de aprender para poder hablar con ellos.

[S6] ¿Es posible que usted me envíe información sobre los precios?
[S7] También tengo algunas preguntas.
[S8] Primero, prefiero una habitación con familia / un piso compartido, no sé cuál es mejor para aprender.
[S9] ¿Es el piso cerca de la escuela?
[S10] Necesito una habitación tranquila para estudiar.
[S11] Segundo, ¿puedo traer mi bicicleta?
[S12] Me gusta montar en bici y quiero explorar las montañas.
[S13] Tercero, soy vegetariano (I'm not picky but I don't eat meat) y espero que la familia pueda cocinar algo para mí.
[S14] Mi novia viene conmigo el primer fin de semana.

[S15] ¿Me puede decir cuándo empiezan los cursos?
[S16] Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo.
[S17] Estoy seguro de que lo voy a pasar muy bien en su escuela.
[S18] Mirando adelante a oír de usted.

[S19] Saludos,
[S20] Daniel Clarke
>>>

First summary: the post as a reader would sum it up to a friend, in two to five short lines (up to seven for a long post), in Spanish, in the post's order. Each line is one thing the writer does (opens, praises one thing, tells what happened, asks one thing, signs off), however many sentences it takes.
Then points: one per summary line, in the same order, and under each point the sentences that develop it as its parts. Each point with its parts covers one run of consecutive sentences: a sentence goes under the line whose run it falls in, even when it touches another line's topic.
- Every sentence goes in exactly one place. A sentence that states a point belongs to that point; the sentences that develop it (an example, a quote, the reason, a question that follows from it) are its parts. Only a sentence doing two clearly separate jobs (a quote, then a question about it) may be listed under two parts.
- When no single sentence states a point (several sentences that together praise one thing, several related questions), the point is a heading over them: sentences [] and its sentences go to its parts.
- An opening and a sign-off are points of their own (even a single word), never one point together.
- text: in Spanish, plain words, at most about fourteen words. What the writer says or does there ("praises how real his inner voice feels", not "inner voice"). A point with sentences of its own says only what those sentences say, not its summary line, since its parts follow right under it; a point that heads its parts (sentences []) says what they add up to. A part says only what it adds.
- kind (parts only), one of: example, quote, reason, explanation, detail, comparison, question, conclusion, context ("detail": anything else that develops the point; "context": background the point needs).
- missing: true for a part a reader here would clearly need and the post leaves out (a claim with no reason at all, a question with nothing to answer it from), with sentences [] and note: one short sentence on what the reader is left without. Only where it really matters; most posts miss nothing.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Spanish.
Reply with JSON only: {"summary":[""],"points":[{"text":"","sentences":[],"parts":[{"kind":"example","text":"","sentences":[2]}]}]}
